source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib path-law transport supplement: A transport estimate gives joint continuity
source_evidence.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). Let \(F\) be a normed additive commutative group, \(U:T\times E\to F\) any field, and \(L\in\mathbb R\). Suppose the bound below holds for every pair \((t,x),(s,y)\). Then \(U\) is jointly continuous. Here \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) denotes the probability couplings. The map \(\operatorname{toReal}\) takes the ordinary real value at finite inputs and sends \(\infty\) to zero; the costs \(Q(t,s)\) here are finite by compactness and the explicit same-sample coupling.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
\(F\) is a normed additive commutative group; no scalar action or completeness is required.
The displayed estimate holds for all pairs in \(T\times E\), with one real constant \(L\). No sign assumption on \(L\), or prior regularity of \(U\), is required.
source_evidence.boundary: The estimate is an explicit input to this general continuity principle. A model application must establish it separately. The proof uses continuity of the extended-real toReal map at zero; no separate finite-cost premise is inserted.

steps.title: Apply the transport limit to the squared cost
steps.text: Fix \(q=(s,y)\). The squared cost is continuous, nonnegative and zero on the diagonal. The preceding theorem, composed with the time projection, gives the transport limit.
steps.assessment: The stated move matches the actual proof and its scope; all required assumptions are already in the public statement or derived internally.

steps.title: Make the majorant tend to zero
steps.text: The real-value map is continuous at the finite value zero, and square root is continuous. The point cost tends to its diagonal value. Adding these terms and multiplying by the fixed real constant gives a vanishing majorant.
steps.assessment: The stated move matches the actual proof and its scope; all required assumptions are already in the public statement or derived internally.

steps.title: Squeeze the norm difference
steps.text: The assumed estimate bounds the nonnegative norm by that majorant. The norm difference tends to zero at every \(q\), which is joint continuity.
